metaDescription: Seven sputnik chandeliers compared on diameter, light count, adjustable rods, semi-flush options, bulb codes and finish, with notes on weight, heat and install.
expertTake: The best all-round pick is the 33 in twelve-light fixture with adjustable rods and a stated diameter. The value pick is the six-light semi-flush at the lowest price tier. Skip a large sputnik in a room with a low ceiling, because the arms spread wide and a fixture of this style needs headroom of at least 7 ft below its lowest point.
introParagraphs: A sputnik chandelier throws metal arms out from a central hub in all directions, with a bulb at the end of each, and it reads as a mid-century classic that suits living rooms, dining rooms and stairwells. The look is bold, but the practical questions are ordinary: diameter, weight, bulb count and the height of your ceiling.

This guide compares seven sputnik chandeliers on diameter, light count, adjustable drop, semi-flush options and bulb requirements. We evaluated each from published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, and we say plainly where a listing gives no weight or ceiling box guidance. Scores are editorial assessments, not measurements.

products.name: RUIYEY 12-Light Sputnik Chandelier, 33.4 in, Gold and Black, Adjustable Height
products.description:
This twelve-light fixture is 33.4 in across with an adjustable hanging height and a two-tone gold and black finish. A stated diameter and a clear light count are the two numbers that matter on a sputnik. Twelve lights give plenty of output for a dining or living area.

The tradeoff is bulb maintenance: twelve sockets mean twelve bulbs to buy and replace, and a fixture of this size is heavy. Compared with the 8-light RUIYEY, it has more lights and a wider spread. The listing states a bulb requirement, which is a useful note.

In a real room, hang the lowest point at least 7 ft above the floor in a walkway and 30 to 36 in above a table. Use LED bulbs for lower heat and check that the ceiling box is rated for the weight. Turn off the breaker before wiring. It suits a dining area or an open living space with a standard or high ceiling. A dimmer is worth adding, since twelve bare bulbs at full brightness can feel harsh in the evening.
products.bestFor: Dining areas and open living spaces with a standard or high ceiling.
pros: Published 33.4 in diameter makes placement simple
Twelve lights give strong output
Adjustable height suits different ceilings
Two-tone gold and black suits many interiors
cons: Twelve bulbs mean more to buy and replace
A large fixture is heavy and needs a rated ceiling box

products.name: Bosceos Modern Sputnik Chandelier, 6-Light Semi-Flush, 22 in Black
products.description:
This semi-flush fixture is 22 in across with six lights in black, designed for rooms with lower ceilings. A semi-flush mount hangs close to the ceiling, so it clears heads in an 8 ft room. It is the cheapest fixture in the comparison.

The tradeoff is that six lights give less output than the twelve-light models, and a short drop gives less control over height. Compared with the RUIYEY, it is smaller and cheaper. A black finish can look heavy in a small room.

For ownership, use LED bulbs and check the box. It suits a low ceiling or a small room. Check the lowest point against the tallest person in the household before you commit. A semi-flush mount is the safest choice where anyone might reach up.
products.bestFor: Rooms with 8 ft ceilings that need a compact semi-flush sputnik.

products.name: MQMQA 12-Light Sputnik Chandelier, 33 in, Pre-Wired, Adjustable Height
products.description:
This twelve-light fixture is 33 in across, pre-wired for easier installation and height adjustable. Pre-wiring means the internal wiring is done, which saves time. It sits in the middle of the price range.

The tradeoff is that pre-wired does not mean plug-in, so the connection to the ceiling still needs care. Compared with the RUIYEY 33.4 in, it is near-identical in size and light count. The finish is ultra-wide in style.

For ownership, use LEDs and check the fixings. It suits a large dining area. Lay the parts out on a clean sheet before you start, so you can match each arm to its socket. Two people make the lift much safer.

products.name: KAISITE Modern Sputnik Chandelier, 8-Light Ceiling Fixture, Height Adjustable
products.description:
This eight-light fixture uses eight medium-base E26 bulbs and has an adjustable height in a mid-century sputnik style. A medium E26 base means you can use standard bulbs. It sits in the lower-middle price range.

The tradeoff is that the data we reviewed gives no diameter, so check the size before ordering. Compared with the twelve-light models, it has a smaller spread and fewer bulbs. Eight lights suit a mid-size room.

For ownership, use LEDs and check the box rating. It suits a living room or a dining area of moderate size. Eight bulbs is a manageable number to keep in stock as spares. A box of matching LEDs avoids a patchwork of tones when one fails.

products.name: MEIXISUE Gold Modern Sputnik Chandelier, 6-Light, Adjustable Branches
products.description:
This six-light gold fixture has adjustable branches and suits a bedroom, stairwell, living room or kitchen, according to the listing. Adjustable branches let you angle the arms to your liking. It is the second cheapest fixture here.

The tradeoff is that adjustable arms can droop or twist over time, and six lights give modest output. Compared with the Bosceos, it has gold arms and adjustable angles. A fixture with adjustable branches needs careful setting.

For ownership, tighten the arm joints after a month. It suits a bedroom or a small living room. Set the arm angles before you add the bulbs, so the sockets do not tilt under their own weight. Revisit the joints after a few weeks of settling.

products.name: Biewalk Modern Sputnik Chandelier, 6-Light, 31.18 in, Pre-Wired
products.description:
This six-light fixture is 31.18 in across and pre-wired for easy assembly, aimed at dining rooms. A 31 in spread with only six lights is airy and open. It is the third cheapest fixture here.

The tradeoff is that six lights over a 31 in span give a sparse look and less output. Compared with the MQMQA, it has half the lights at a similar width. A sparse look suits some rooms better.

For ownership, use bright LEDs and check the box. It suits a dining room where a light, airy fixture is wanted. It pairs well with a round or square table where the arms reach out evenly. Over a long rectangular table, a linear fixture is a better match.

products.name: YIHANTLZ 12-Light Milk Glass Bubble Chandelier, 40 in Sputnik
products.description:
This twelve-light fixture is 40 in across with frosted milk glass bubbles on a metal frame. Glass globes make the sputnik shape softer and more decorative. It is the most expensive fixture in the comparison.

The tradeoff is price and weight: twelve glass bubbles on a 40 in frame are heavy, and a ceiling box must be rated for them. Compared with the metal-only RUIYEY, it is far more decorative. Glass is also fragile in transit.

For ownership, hang with two people and use LED bulbs. It suits a large room with a high ceiling. Unpack the glass bubbles last and keep the packing material until the fixture is hung. A spare bubble is not likely to be supplied, so handle them gently.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Add the room's length and width in feet, and use the total as the fixture diameter in inches as a starting guide. The RUIYEY at 33.4 in suits a dining table, the Bosceos at 22 in a small room. The lowest point must clear heads. Over a table, keep the fixture at least 12 in narrower than the table so that heads do not bump the arms.

Twelve lights give strong output but need twelve bulbs, six suit a smaller room. The KAISITE lists E26 bulbs. Use LED bulbs for lower heat and check the socket tag. A fixture with many bulbs also gives a sparkle that suits a party but feels bright for quiet evenings, so a dimmer helps. Matching bulbs across all sockets keeps the glow even.

A semi-flush, as on the Bosceos, suits an 8 ft ceiling. A drop with adjustable rods suits higher ceilings. Choose by ceiling height and clearance. If you are between the two, choose semi-flush for safety and add table lamps for atmosphere.

Gold, black and two-tone finishes change the mood. Glass bubbles, as on the YIHANTLZ, soften the look. Match the finish to your other fittings. A finish that matches the cabinet handles and tap in the room looks deliberate and calm. Black and gold are both easy to match with other fittings.

A large sputnik can be heavy, so the ceiling box must be rated for it. Most listings give no weight. Ask an electrician to check, and turn off the breaker before wiring. A heavy fixture on an old plastic box is a real risk, so upgrade the box if in doubt.

Arms loosen, finishes tarnish and bulbs fail. No independent source documents lifespan for these fixtures. Check the arms each year and dust the bulbs. Keep a note of the bulb type and a few spares in a drawer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated sizes
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each listing states diameter. The RUIYEY, Bosceos and Biewalk do. Missing figures count against a pick. Diameter is the most useful number for a sputnik.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light count and bulbs
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted light counts and bulb codes. Standard bulbs earn credit. We did not measure output. We treat light counts as claims, not measured output.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mount and ceiling fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared semi-flush and drop designs against ceiling heights. Good fit scores higher. Scores are editorial. Semi-flush options earned credit for low rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install and weight clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted whether listings explain weight and wiring. Missing detail counts against a pick. We could not verify installation. Weight guidance is rare in these listings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read patterns in owner feedback on loose arms, finish and bulb counts. These themes recur in the category. We do not publish ratings or review counts. Loose arms were the most common complaint.

maintenance.why: Dust dims light and gathers on arms. A dry cloth keeps it clear. Switch off and let the bulbs cool first. A soft brush reaches between the arms.
Joints loosen with use. Tighten them to prevent droop. Use a ladder with a helper.
One dark bulb unbalances the look. Replace with matching LEDs. Keep spare matching bulbs.
A loose canopy exposes wiring. Tighten it with the power off. Turn off the breaker before touching any wires.
Gold and black show fingerprints. A dry cloth keeps them clean. Avoid abrasive cloths on plating. A soft dry cloth is enough for most days.

faq.q: What size sputnik chandelier do I need?
faq.a: Add the room's length and width in feet, and use the total in inches as a starting guide. Adjust for the table and ceiling. Then check the result against the room's ceiling height.

faq.q: How high should I hang it?
faq.a: At least 7 ft above the floor in a walkway and 30 to 36 in above a table. A lower fixture suits a smaller room. Hang it higher if the room has a tall ceiling, but keep light within reach of the table.
A hardwired fixture needs a rated ceiling box and the power off. Ask an electrician if unsure. Never work on live wires. A ceiling box rated for the weight is essential.
LED bulbs that fit the socket, such as E26. Check the socket's maximum wattage. Warm white suits living rooms. Match all bulbs so that the glow is even.

faq.q: Is a semi-flush sputnik an option for low ceilings?
faq.a: Yes, a semi-flush hangs close to the ceiling. It clears heads in an 8 ft room. A semi-flush may be a better fit than a drop. Sputniks with a drop need at least a nine foot ceiling to look right.

Many last years, but arms loosen and finishes tarnish. No independent source documents lifespan. A longer warranty is a practical durability sign. Keep spare arms or screws if the maker supplies them.
